references.text: Delilah cries out the same warning, 'The Philistines are upon you, Samson!', as a recurring pattern in the story of Samson's trials.
The same warning from Delilah to Samson about the Philistine attack, illustrating the repeated pattern of deception.
Samson wakes again from his sleep, but this time he has lost his strength, showing the consequence of his repeated mistakes.
The Philistines shout against Samson in a previous confrontation, demonstrating the enduring hostility between them.
The immediate context where Delilah weaves Samson's hair into the loom, which leads directly to this event involving the peg and the weaving.
